speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The first category relates to amendments to put in place the tax treatment for variable capital companies (VCCs).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The second category relates to amendments to the VCC Act which was passed by Parliament in October last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The VCC is a corporate structure incorporated under the VCC Act which may only be used as an investment fund vehicle.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It has features that are tailored for this purpose.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For example, a VCC may vary its share capital without seeking investors' approval, and may pay dividends using profit or capital.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The shareholders of a VCC are the fund investors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A VCC must be managed by a fund manager that is regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS).

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Introducing the VCC will increase the value proposition for fund managers to domicile their investment funds in Singapore and complements our existing efforts to anchor fund management and other related activities here.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It will also create new business opportunities for lawyers, accountants, tax advisors, fund administrators and custodians in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The first category of amendments deals with the tax treatment for VCCs through amendments to the Income Tax Act, Goods and Services Tax (GST) Act and Stamp Duties Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The proposed tax treatment, which was formulated in consultation with industry, recognises the unique characteristics of a VCC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: A key feature of a VCC is its ability to combine the advantage of a single legal entity at the umbrella VCC fund level, with segregation of assets and liabilities at the sub-fund level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The salient aspects of the Corporate Income Tax treatment for a VCC are as follows.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Deductions and allowances for expenses incurred by an umbrella VCC will be applied at the sub-fund level to determine the sub-fund's chargeable income.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Where applicable, a VCC will enjoy the startup or partial tax exemption under our general Corporate Income Tax regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These exemptions will be enjoyed once at the umbrella VCC level, regardless of the number of sub-funds under the umbrella VCC or the number of sub-funds that are subsequently added to the umbrella VCC.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These incentives will provide tax exemption on qualifying investment income.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As for the GST treatment of VCCs, GST will be applicable at the sub-fund level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: GST accounting and reporting are to be performed separately by each sub-fund that is liable for GST registration.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This is because sub-funds have segregated assets and liabilities, and each sub-fund makes independent sale and purchase decisions based on its investment mandate.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: On stamp duty treatment of VCCs, stamp duty is levied at the sub-fund level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: For instance, stamp duty will be levied on an instrument that transfers the interest in property and shares between sub-funds.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This treatment regards sub-funds as separate persons for stamp duty purposes and is in line with the principle that sub-funds have segregated assets and liabilities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRAS will provide further guidance and details of the tax treatment for VCCs on its website and e-Tax Guides.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The second category of amendments seeks to amend two aspects of the VCC Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The first aspect relates to the insolvency provisions in the VCC Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The current provisions in the VCC Act relating to the receivership and winding up of VCCs and their sub-funds are adapted from the Companies Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In October 2018, the Insolvency, Restructuring and Dissolution Act (IRDA) was passed by Parliament.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: IRDA consolidates all personal and corporate insolvency and debt restructuring laws under one statute.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: When IRDA comes into force, the insolvency provisions in the Companies Act will be repealed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This will align the insolvency regime for VCCs and their sub-funds with that of other corporate structures in Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: I had previously highlighted the need for these amendments when I moved the VCC Bill in Parliament last year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This was also highlighted in the explanatory brief accompanying the VCC Bill on the MAS website, as well as during the most recent public consultation on the operational framework for VCCs in July this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The second aspect involves technical amendments to the VCC Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: One example is to clarify that a VCC should have at least one member.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This aligns the minimum number of members in a VCC with that for companies under the Companies Act.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Other amendments include requiring documentary evidence of the directors' decision to be lodged with the Registrar for proper records for alterations to the VCC constitution that do not require a members' resolution.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: These have been included for clarity, in light of enquiries received.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: The Bill will provide clarity to fund managers who are looking to domicile funds as VCCs when the VCC framework becomes operational at the end of this year, first, in terms of the tax treatment for VCCs and, second, in terms of the receivership and winding-up framework applicable to VCCs and their sub-funds.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The VCC structure is designed to encourage investors to place their funds in Singapore and strengthen Singapore's economy.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: I note that there are several amendments to the VCC Act and they may be broadly classified into two areas: first, amendments to the VCC to align the VCC insolvency regime with all the other corporate structures in Singapore; and second, other more technical amendments.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: However, my questions today revolve more so around the development and progress of the VCC Framework since it was introduced last year, in particular, the impact of the VCC Framework on the economy and job market and prospects in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: The Second Minister for Finance, Ms Indranee Rajah mentioned in Parliament last year, that the VCC framework will create new business opportunities for lawyers, accountants, tax advisors, fund administrators and custodians in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In this respect, I have the following questions.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: First, it has been about one year since the passing of the VCC Act.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: As a follow-up question, are they all in the legal/accounting sector?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Would the Minister be able to provide a brief breakdown of the new jobs created within the various sectors?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Second, I note that the VCC framework is a relatively new corporate structure introduced last year, which is unlike the traditional company.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: How well received is the VCC structure in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Has it achieved its objective in making Singapore a more attractive fund management hub?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In the workforce: are there also plans to provide education and training to the fund managers, lawyers and accountants who would be advising and assisting with VCCs?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: In the educational institutions, are there also plans to introduce this VCC framework into the local law schools and universities, as part of their Corporate Law modules, to prepare local law students for the possibility of working with the VCC framework, for example, drafting of fund documents, knowing the VCC requirements and so on?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Could more be done to prepare and ensure that our students and workers are able to be adept and competent with handling the VCC framework?

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
text: Third, there are indications that the Singapore economy is headed towards uncertain territory.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government is working on the Subsidiary Legislation which sets out the operational framework for VCCs and their sub-funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The tax treatment for VCCs will also be introduced, which I have just dealt with in my speech earlier.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: As such I will begin by addressing Mr Patrick Tay's second question on reception of the VCC structure, and the plans to prepare the industry and the educational institutions for the launch of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The response to the VCC framework from the asset management industry both in Singapore and abroad has been positive, with the VCC being hailed as a "game changer".

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It has been welcomed as a positive step to enhance the suite of fund structuring options in Singapore with a structure that is fit for use as an investment fund vehicle.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: It is also an important step to ensure that Singapore remains competitive with other long-established fund domiciles, such as Luxembourg and Ireland.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS has been actively promoting the VCC framework to three main groups: first, the fund managers; second, investors; and third, service providers, including lawyers, accountants, tax advisors, fund administrators and custodians.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: When I moved the VCC Bill last year, I mentioned that MAS has been working closely with industry associations, local service providers and consultants to familiarise them with the value proposition and features of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These include providing greater flexibility in the use of capital, allowing fund managers to consolidate certain administrative functions to achieve cost efficiencies, and allowing for funds domiciled in other jurisdictions to redomicile to Singapore as VCCs.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Since last year, MAS has continued with its engagements with the industry to familiarise it with the features of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS participated in various industry-led events and seminars, including the Seminar on the VCC Act organised by the Law Society of Singapore in April this year.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS continues to conduct regular engagement sessions with fund managers and other service providers to ensure that they are kept abreast of the developments and timeline for the implementation of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS has also recently concluded two promotional trips to North America and Japan to encourage fund managers and investors to consider the VCC as a viable structuring option for their investment funds.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: During these overseas trips, MAS also met with fund service providers to familiarise them with the VCC framework, so that they can, in time, introduce the VCC as a structuring option for their clients.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: MAS received positive feedback on the VCC framework, and many of the stakeholders that were engaged are keen to explore domiciling funds in Singapore when the framework is launched.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In addition, MAS officers continue to participate in panel discussions and seminars in New York and London to educate the local asset management community about the features of the VCC framework.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: These fund managers will be able to have their funds registered as VCCs on the day that the VCC framework is launched.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Interested fund managers and service providers may approach MAS to find out more about participation.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We will monitor its impact on the Singapore economy once the framework is launched.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: I would add, however, that the introduction of VCC is one important piece, but not the only piece in our plan for Singapore to be the leading pan-Asian hub for fund domiciliation and management.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government continues to work in tandem with the industry to refine our existing schemes and introduce new initiatives to foster the development of the asset management industry.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Government will continue to work with the industry to ensure that all players in the industry are fully apprised of this new structuring option and are equipped to take advantage of its features as well as the new business opportunities that it can provide.
